theory.intro: Compare fractions using equal-sized shapes divided into equal parts (area models), or by writing the fraction of each collection (discrete models). For equal-sized wholes, the larger shaded area represents the larger fraction. For collections with matching totals, compare the marked counts.
facts: For a collection, write $\frac{\text{marked objects}}{\text{total objects}}$. When the totals match, the collection with more marked objects has the greater marked fraction.
steps: For area models, check that the wholes are equal-sized and each partition has equal parts. For collections, count the marked objects and check that the total objects match.
Write the fractions. If the area models have different denominators, use equivalent fractions with a common denominator, subdividing the models when useful.
Compare the numerators once the denominators match. Write $<$, $>$ or $=$.

workedExamples.solution_text:
a. A has $1$ of $6$ equal parts shaded, so it shows $\frac{1}{6}$. B has $5$ of $6$ shaded, so it shows $\frac{5}{6}$.
$\frac{1}{6}<\frac{5}{6}$
B has the greater shaded fraction.
b. The shaded area depends on the size of the whole. Equal-sized bars let the shaded areas show the comparison of the fractions.

A has $4$ of $6$ equal parts shaded: $\frac{4}{6}$. B has $2$ of $3$ equal parts shaded: $\frac{2}{3}$.
Splitting each third of B into two equal parts gives $4$ shaded sixths.
$\frac{2}{3}=\frac{4}{6}$
The shaded areas are equal.

P has $2$ of $4$ equal parts shaded: $\frac{2}{4}$.
Q has $3$ of $8$ equal parts shaded: $\frac{3}{8}$.
Splitting each quarter of P into two equal parts gives $4$ shaded eighths.
$\frac{2}{4}=\frac{4}{8}$
$\frac{4}{8}>\frac{3}{8}$
P has the greater shaded fraction. Counting only shaded parts is not enough because the parts have different sizes.

workedExamples.question_text: Two equal-sized bars are divided into equal parts. Bar A has $1$ of $4$ parts shaded. Bar B has $1$ of $8$ parts shaded. Which has the greater shaded area?
workedExamples.solution_text:
Splitting each quarter into two equal parts gives eighths.
$\frac{1}{4}=\frac{2}{8}$
$\frac{2}{8}>\frac{1}{8}$
Bar A has the greater shaded area. One quarter is larger than one eighth of the same-sized whole.

workedExamples.question_text: Collection A has $10$ counters, with $4$ marked. Collection B has $10$ counters, with $7$ marked. Write and compare the marked fractions.
workedExamples.solution_text:
A has $4$ marked counters out of $10$: $\frac{4}{10}$.
B has $7$ marked counters out of $10$: $\frac{7}{10}$.
$\frac{4}{10}<\frac{7}{10}$
The totals match, so compare the marked counts. Collection B has the greater marked fraction.

foundation.solution_text:
Bar A shows $\frac{2}{5}$ and bar B shows $\frac{4}{5}$.
$\frac{4}{5}>\frac{2}{5}$

foundation.question_text:
In two equal collections of $12$ counters, $3$ are red in collection P and $7$ are red in collection Q.
Compare the red fractions.

One equal-sized rectangle has $\frac{1}{3}$ shaded and another has $\frac{1}{6}$ shaded.
Which shaded area is larger?

A set has $8$ stars with $4$ coloured.
Another equal-sized set has $8$ stars with $6$ coloured.
Write and compare the fractions.
foundation.solution_text:
$\frac{4}{8}<\frac{6}{8}$
The second set has the greater coloured fraction.

foundation.question_text:
Two equal circles show $\frac{3}{4}$ and $\frac{5}{8}$ shaded.
Which is greater?
True or false: in equal wholes, shading $2$ of $6$ equal parts is more than shading $1$ of $3$ equal parts.
foundation.solution_text:
$\frac{2}{6}=\frac{1}{3}$
The statement is **false**; the areas are equal.

development.question_text:
Two equal-sized bars are divided into equal parts.
Bar A has $7$ of $10$ parts shaded.
Bar B has $4$ of $5$ parts shaded.
Which has the greater shaded fraction?
development.solution_text:
$\frac{4}{5}=\frac{8}{10}$
$\frac{8}{10}>\frac{7}{10}$
Bar B has the greater shaded fraction.

development.question_text:
An area model split into twelfths has $8$ parts shaded.
Compare the shaded fractions with an equal-sized model split into thirds with $2$ parts shaded.

Two equal-sized bars are divided into equal parts. Bar A has $3$ of $4$ parts shaded and bar B has $5$ of $8$ parts shaded.
A student says B has the greater shaded fraction because $5>3$.
Correct the claim.
development.solution_text:
$\frac{3}{4}=\frac{6}{8}$
$\frac{6}{8}>\frac{5}{8}$
Bar A has the greater shaded fraction. The eighths in B are smaller than the quarters in A, so comparing only shaded counts is not enough.

development.question_text:
Two equal-sized strips are divided into equal parts.
The first has $7$ of $8$ parts shaded and the second has $3$ of $4$ parts shaded.
Which represents the greater shaded fraction?
development.solution_text:
$\frac{3}{4}=\frac{6}{8}$
$\frac{7}{8}>\frac{6}{8}$
The first strip represents the greater shaded fraction.

development.question_text:
Collection A has $15$ counters with $7$ marked.
Collection B has $15$ counters with $11$ marked.
Write and compare the marked fractions.
development.solution_text:
A: $\frac{7}{15}$
B: $\frac{11}{15}$
$\frac{7}{15}<\frac{11}{15}$
Collection B has the greater marked fraction.

development.question_text: Explain why area models must use equal-sized wholes when comparing $\frac{3}{4}$ and $\frac{2}{3}$.
development.solution_text:
The shaded area depends on the size of the whole.
Equal-sized wholes let the fractions themselves determine the comparison.

mastery.question_text:
Two equal-sized rectangles are divided into equal parts.
Rectangle A has $11$ of $16$ parts shaded.
Rectangle B has $5$ of $8$ parts shaded.
Write and compare the shaded fractions.
mastery.solution_text:
A: $\frac{11}{16}$
B: $\frac{5}{8}=\frac{10}{16}$
$\frac{11}{16}>\frac{10}{16}$
Rectangle A has the greater shaded fraction.

mastery.question_text:
Equal-sized area models are divided into equal parts.
Model A has $9$ shaded parts out of $12$.
Model B has $7$ shaded parts out of $12$.
Which represents the greater fraction?
mastery.solution_text:
Both models are divided into twelfths.
$\frac{9}{12}>\frac{7}{12}$
Model A represents the greater fraction.

mastery.question_text:
Two equal-area rectangles are partitioned differently.
One shows $\frac{4}{6}$ shaded and the other $\frac{6}{9}$.
Decide whether either is greater.
mastery.solution_text:
$\frac{4}{6}=\frac{2}{3}$
$\frac{6}{9}=\frac{2}{3}$
Neither is greater; the shaded areas are equal.
